issues.competing_evidence: Reimers+99 assigns 60/68 MG from n=2/3 harmonics with no formal errors. Vogel+07 phase-resolved slab model gives 61.4/69.6 MG with typical ±0.5 MG model parameter uncertainty under fixed i=70° and coupled geometry/plasma assumptions. Tutar Özdarcan+17 2015 spectropolarimetry gives 49 MG at one spot and 69/104/207 MG alternatives at the other depending on harmonic number; no formal field errors. These values are not a radio-region or photospheric mean field.
issues.why_it_matters: Local field/spot assignment affects comparisons of magnetic-field strength and topology across magnetic CVs; choosing one set would conceal model and harmonic ambiguity.
issues.needed_action: Inspect/re-fit the published phase-resolved circular-polarization spectra using the competing harmonic identifications and clarify whether the changes reflect state/geometry or a prior model assumption. Keep all measurements separately until an explicit preferred solution is justified; no value averaging.

issues.parameter: System taxonomy and Roche-lobe transfer state
issues.competing_evidence: Reimers+99 and Schwarz+01 describe a low-accretion polar/LARP. Vogel+07 finds a synchronized polar but argues donor likely underfills its lobe and proposes a detached wind-fed post-common-envelope/pre-polar interpretation; no direct fill factor is measured. The 2017 article continues to call WX LMi a polar/LARP.
issues.why_it_matters: Catalog class describes observed magnetic accretion, while evolutionary interpretation determines whether it is counted among interacting RLO CVs or detached/pre-polar binaries. Treating one as the other could bias population comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Choose a catalog taxonomy that keeps confirmed magnetic polar/LARP identity separate from proposed detached/pre-polar evolution (recommended dual labels); confirm that no later donor/Roche geometry measurement supersedes Vogel+07.

issues.competing_evidence: Vogel+07 Eq. 1 fits 1999–2005 photometric maxima and RV phase, P_orb=0.11592364(43) d. Reimers+99 preliminary 0.11638 d used just over one cycle. Tutar Özdarcan+17 gives Hα fit 0.097±0.007 d from one 2015 cycle and explicitly says periods/synchronization are inconclusive; it notes cyclotron features vary with spin but no definitive separate spin period.
issues.why_it_matters: Period confusion propagates into orbital evolution, spin state and donor-sequence comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Check the 2017 velocity/polarization phase fit and any erratum or follow-up data for a cycle-count/fit issue; meanwhile retain Vogel+07 Porb as preferred and leave Pspin/beat blank absent an independent measurement.

issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 3 reports 8.7e−15 (1–10 keV) and 4.2e−14 erg cm−2 s−1 (0.1–10 keV), citing Vogel+07. Vogel+07 Table 4 gives a preferred two-MEKAL unabsorbed 0.1–5 keV flux of 5.4e−14; its unacceptable single-MEKAL fit has 4.2e−14 in 0.1–5 keV. Ridder+23 does not document the source-specific conversion model in the table.
issues.why_it_matters: The model/band ambiguity changes X-ray luminosity and radio/X-ray comparisons; equating the same number across different bands would misstate the spectrum.
issues.needed_action: Reproduce the two Ridder+23 fluxes with the stated PIMMS/model approach using the original preferred two-MEKAL fit and N_H, then confirm whether 4.2e−14 is an accidental carry-over from the rejected single-MEKAL fit. Until then retain each with its published band/model and do not choose or average.
